verdict.rationale: Kitty has its own documented remote-control interface that can be driven from scripts or the shell prompt. It can open new windows, send arbitrary text to any window, and change window and tab titles "etc."; tabs, splits and layouts are described as programmable, and an official CLI is documented. However, nothing shows that remote control covers every UI action, such as the full set of mappable actions, so UI parity is implied rather than proven. Missing for 10: documented parity mapping between all mappable UI actions and remote-control commands, coverage of config and theme changes through the API, and independent hands-on corroboration of full parity.
